scope: Theorem 5.2 of the manuscript “Abundance in numerical dimension one for terminal threefolds in positive characteristic” (preprints/Abundance-in-numerical-dimension-one-for-terminal-threefolds-in-positive-characteristic-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 035 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 5e170f2c29b7026e), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 32. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For the prepared data and periods fixed above, let E be a vector bundle on V with the following properties: (i) χ(P1 i (E)) = 0 for every integer i. (ii) For J = E, E!, the spaces H0(V, J(nD)/J) have dimensions bounded independently of the positive integer n. (iii) For J = E, E! there is a constant AJ such that g0 ue (i; J) > 0 =⇒ dist(i, MeZ) ≤ AJ for all sufficiently large e. Then global sections of ER form a finite-dimensional k-vector space. Every Laurent Čech 1-cocycle on a finite affine cover adapted to the bundles and the divisor has an actual Laurent primitive. The same assertion holds after refining such a cover.
